controls.label: Expected glow
controls.qualification: An estimate, not a measurement: black-body color at 1,390 K, the bare-rock maximum for its orbit.
controls.notes: Nobody has measured Wolf 327 b's heat. This is the color of a black body at 1,390 K, the hottest day side a dark, airless rock can have on its orbit (computed from wolf-327's temperature, 3542 K, and the orbit's a/R* 5.3, as T* (R*/a)^(1/2) (2/3)^(1/4)). Nine rocky planets of red dwarfs with a measured day side fall within 13% of this kind of estimate (Coy et al. 2025); GJ 357 b, measured since, is 35% above it. Its star lights the day side. Reflected starlight is not included.

charts.alt: The orbits of Wolf 327's planets in this map from above, to scale, with Wolf 327 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

Wolf 327 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 2 sectors (21, 48) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 4918918, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 4-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
